input: Enroll in a night class on urban history

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Urban history is broad — knowing whether they want a specific era, city, region, or theme (e.g., housing, race, planning) narrows which courses actually fit.
Their geographic location determines which local colleges, universities, or community centers offer relevant in-person night classes.
Whether they want an in-person, hybrid, or fully online night class fundamentally changes where to look and what to enroll in.
Knowing which nights of the week they are free and how long the course can run affects which class schedules are viable.
Tuition costs vary enormously between community colleges, university continuing education, and private programs — budget determines which options are realistic.
Whether they want a credit-bearing course (for a degree), a professional certificate, or a casual enrichment class shapes which institutions and programs to target.
Understanding what they want to walk away with — a credential, specific knowledge, networking, or personal enrichment — defines what a successful enrollment looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Enroll in a night class on urban history
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and enroll in a night class focused on urban history.

questions.title: What specific aspect of urban history interests you most?
questions.description: Identify whether the user wants a broad urban history survey or a focused topic such as a specific city, era, or theme like urban planning, housing, or immigration.

questions.title: What city or region are you located in?
questions.description: Determine the user's location to identify nearby colleges, universities, or community centers offering relevant in-person night classes.

questions.title: Do you prefer in-person, hybrid, or fully online?
questions.description: Clarify the desired class format, which determines whether to search local institutions or online platforms.

questions.title: Which nights of the week are you available to attend?
questions.description: Identify the user's weekly schedule availability to filter classes by viable meeting days and times.

questions.title: What is your budget for tuition or course fees?
questions.description: Establish a spending limit to determine whether to focus on free, low-cost community college options or higher-priced university programs.

questions.title: Do you need this class to count for academic credit?
questions.description: Determine whether the user requires a credit-bearing course, a certificate, or is happy with a non-credit enrichment class, which affects which institutions to target.

questions.title: What do you most want to walk away with after the course?
questions.description: Understand the user's primary goal — a credential, deeper knowledge, professional development, or social connection — to define what a successful outcome looks like.
